text: Over 500M SAND Minted in Suspected The Sandbox Security Breach; Upbit Issues Warning, Bithumb Suspends Transfers Major metaverse project The Sandbox is suspected of suffering a serious security breach on Base, with an attacker reportedly gaining token minting permissions and being able to mint SAND arbitrarily. Onchain data shows that more than 500 million SAND have been minted so far, with the activity still ongoing. The Sandbox is an Animoca Brands subsidiary and raised $93 million in a 2021 funding round. South Korea's two largest crypto exchanges, Upbit and Bithumb, have both taken precautionary measures. Upbit issued a trading caution for SAND, while Bithumb temporarily suspended SAND deposits and withdrawals. Upbit said it identified signs of a potential security issue involving SAND on August 22 and warned users of heightened price volatility. According to PeckShield monitoring, The Sandbox appears to have been exploited, with approximately 14.9 billion SAND minted across two addresses. The Sandbox has yet to publicly clarify the cause or full scope of the incident. The Sandbox said it has fully contained a vulnerability affecting the SAND cross-chain bridge on Base and BNB Smart Chain (BSC). An attacker minted unbacked SAND on both networks, and bridging has since been disabled. The incident affected less than 0.01% of SAND's total supply, while SAND on Ethereum and Polygon, user wallets, and Ethereum-locked backing assets remain unaffected. The team is preparing a compensation plan for eligible affected LP users and advised users not to trade SAND on Base or BSC. — link
